sheet.summary: According to the Skanda Purana's Lonar Mahatmya and local legend, the crater formed when Lord Vishnu manifested as Daityasudana to tear open the underworld and destroy the demon Lonasura, leaving a depression filled with the demon's saline blood. Geological and archaeological investigations confirmed that the site is actually a 1.8-kilometre-wide hypervelocity meteorite impact crater carved into basalt, harboring a hyper-alkaline soda lake that turned dramatically pink in June 2020 due to an explosive bloom of Haloarchaea microbes. Geochemists remain sharply divided over the crater's antiquity, with thermoluminescence estimates dating the impact to roughly 52,000 years ago while newer argon-argon isotopic measurements place it much earlier at approximately 570,000 years ago. It remains unknown whether unvaporized remnants of the metallic or chondritic meteorite survive buried beneath the lake sediments, as well as the exact subterranean origin of the freshwater springs feeding the crater's rim.
